title: Taasko kasvun väärä hälytys? – Taloustieteilijä uskoo korkojen ja energian hinnan iskevän Suomen kasvulukuihin
content:
Pääministeri Petteri Orpo sanoo tänään julkaistujen työllisyyslukujen olevan ”synkkä päivä kaikille opposition pessimisteille”. Osa taloustieteilijöistä näkee perustellun syyn pessimismiin.

Tilastokeskus kertoi työllisten määrän kasvaneen elokuussa 34 000 hengellä viime vuoteen verrattuna. Joko uskaltaa sanoa, että työllisyys on oikeasti lähtenyt kasvuun, Pellervon taloustutkimuksen tutkimusjohtaja ja Vaasan yliopiston taloustieteen professori Olli-Pekka Ruuskanen?

– En vielä poksauttaisi samppanjapulloa. Talouden ja työllisyyden kasvu on ollut vasta maltillinen, ei mikään merkittävä kasvusysäys, Olli-Pekka Ruuskanen varoittaa.

Vaikka kotimaan taloudessa on nyt tapahtunut myönteistä värinää, globaali kehitys potkii sitä vastaan. Ruuskanen pelkää kohoavien korkojen ja energian hinnan iskevään kovaa Suomen kasvulukuihin.

Hän arvioi alkusyksyn talouskeskustelun ”lähteneen vähän lapasesta, kun media on täynnä juttuja kovasta talouskasvusta”.

Tällä viikolla ehdittiin iloita hyvien työllisyyslukujen lisäksi myös valtiovarainministeriön talouden kasvuennusteista. VM ennusti tälle vuodelle Suomen talouteen 1,6 ja ensi vuodelle 2,8 prosentin kasvua.

title: No further than the idea stage: defence start-ups struggle to secure start-up funding
content:
Once a company has demonstrated the potential of its technology and development begins to accelerate, securing funding becomes relatively easy. Getting to this point is much harder, meaning that many start-ups never get beyond the idea stage because they lack funding.

For defence-sector companies to develop rapidly, money is needed not only when they have already achieved their first successes, but also at the very beginning – to develop the idea, build a prototype and test the technology. Yet, the funding currently available falls far short of covering all companies’ needs. This means that a promising idea may never progress beyond the initial stage – not because it lacks potential, but because the company does not have sufficient resources to demonstrate that potential.

title: Armin Robber, Rapper and Organizer of Music Meetups, Arrested
content:
According to HRANA, Armin, known as “Armin Robber,” a rapper, was arrested by security forces.

Following his arrest, the singer was transferred to an undisclosed location.

He also recently attended a rap-related gathering, known as a “rap meetup,” in one of the country’s cities. A review of his activities indicates that in recent years he has played a role in organizing and overseeing such gatherings in various cities, including Tehran, Karaj, Gilan, and Kermanshah.

Numerous videos of these gatherings and rap performances have been published on pages and channels associated with Armin Robber’s activities. Among them, videos from an “Armin Robber meetup” were published in April 2026. Images from similar events attended by him in Kermanshah and several other locations across the country had also previously been published.

As of the time of this report, no precise information has been obtained regarding the location or circumstances of his arrest or the charges brought against him.

title: South African Women Need Protection, Not Warnings
content:
The discovery of several women’s bodies on the outskirts of South Africa’s commercial capital, Johannesburg, has caused fear, anxiety and outrage across the country. All the women were found naked or partially clothed, according to police. Some of the bodies had bruising.

At least three suspects are already in custody as authorities continue to examine possible links between the killings.

These mysterious killings of women are not isolated crimes but part of a longstanding crisis about gender-based violence in South Africa. Earlier in 2026, Human Rights Watch noted that systemic criminal justice failures impede women in South Africa from accessing justice, while survivors have limited access to psychosocial support. Human Rights Watch has also documented that sex workers, LGBT people, and undocumented women face additional barriers to protection and redress.

The South African Medical Research Council has in the past, estimated that nearly seven women were killed each day in the country, including three by an intimate partner. Police failed to identify a suspect in about 44 percent of cases.

title: EU and Canada to unveil new partnership, but it may not be ‘associate membership,’ says ambassador
content:
Ottawa and Brussels will announce a comprehensive set of partnerships within the coming year, but the shape of the future relationship is still up for discussion, Canada’s ambassador to the EU said Tuesday.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced during her State of the Union speech last week that the door would be open to Canada becoming “the first associate member” of the EU. But Ottawa has played down the formal nature of that arrangement.

“It was enormously gratifying for Canada to hear that from the president because I think it reflects the fact that Europeans see Canada in the same way that we see Europe,” Jonathan Wilkinson told POLITICO’s Brussels Playbook Live Summit.

“Ultimately, I’m less fussed about what we end up calling it. I’m more fussed about that we have initiatives that are really going to drive prosperity, economic security, and a range of things moving forward,” he said.

title: Varsinais-Suomessa on nyt yli 500 000 asukasta
content:
Varsinais-Suomi vahvistaa asemaansa asukasluvultaan Suomen kolmanneksi suurimpana maakuntana ja nopeimmin kasvavien joukossa. Maakunnan asukasluku ylitti Tilastokeskuksen ennakkotietojen mukaan elokuussa puolen miljoonan asukkaan rajan. Tarkka luku oli elokuun lopussa 500 321.

Väestö kasvoi vuoden takaisesta 3 309 asukkaalla, mikä oli toiseksi nopein kasvuvauhti heti Uudenmaan jälkeen. Varsinais-Suomen kasvu on ollut viime vuosina hyvin nopeaa.

– Varsinais-Suomi on saanut 2020-luvulla 10 000 uutta asukasta kolmen vuoden välein ja edellisen 30 vuoden aikana maakunta on kasvanut lähes koko Kainuun asukasluvun verran, havainnollistaa tietopalvelupäällikkö Antti Vasanen Varsinais-Suomen liitosta.

Varsinais-Suomen asukaslukua kasvattaa muuttovoitto sekä ulkomailta että muualta Suomesta. Nettomaahanmuutto kasvatti Varsinais-Suomen väestöä noin 3 250 asukkaalla edelliseen vuoteen verrattuna ja kotimainen nettomuuttoliike 1 450 asukkaalla.

Ilman muuttovoittoa Varsinais-Suomen asukasluku laskisi, sillä maakunnassa kuolee vuosittain yli tuhat ihmistä enemmän kuin syntyy. Myös syntyvyys on kohentunut hieman kuluvan vuoden aikana.

title: ”Hyvä digipalvelu poistaa työtä, huono siirtää tehtäviä” – Software Finland hakee Suomen parhaita digipalveluita, jotka poistavat turhauttavaa digikitkaa
content:
Suomalaista ohjelmistoteollisuutta edustava Software Finland ry palkitsee jälleen Suomen parhaat digipalvelut. Ehdokashaku on nyt avoinna ja voittajat julkistetaan 5.11.2026. Tuomariston suurennuslasin alla ovat erityisesti selkeys, tuottavuus ja vaikuttavuus.

”Digitalisoitu on, mutta kitkaa riittää”, tuomariston puheenjohtajana toimiva suomalaisen ohjelmistoalan vaikuttaja Riitta Raesmaa kiteyttää.

”Digitaalisia palveluita on rakennettu vuosikymmeniä ja tuottavuus on noussut, mutta ei läheskään niin paljon kuin odotimme. Jos digitaalinen palvelu ei vähennä työtä vaan siirtää tehtäviä omalta organisaatiolta asiakkaille, rima on liian matalalla”, Raesmaa paaluttaa.

Vuoden Digipalvelu -tunnustus myönnetään tänä vuonna jo kahdeksatta kertaa, ja uutta on jako kahteen kategoriaan. Palkinto annetaan parhaalle palvelulle sekä yksityiseltä että julkiselta sektorilta. Palvelut voivat olla suunnattuja joko yksityisille käyttäjille tai organisaatioille: olennaista on, että ne poistavat digikitkaa ja lisäävät tuottavuutta.

Ohjelmistoalan ammattilaisista koostuvan 11-henkisen tuomariston arviointikriteerit on jaoteltu käyttäjän näkökulmaan ja ohjelmisto-osaamiseen. Käytön osalta arvioidaan muun muassa, miten palvelu on lisännyt käyttäjiensä hyvinvointia, tuonut heille iloa, vapauttanut aikaa tai ratkaissut ongelmia. Teknisessä vaakakupissa painavat muun muassa kestävyys, vastuullisuus, innovatiivisuus, toteutuksen laatu ja tietoturva.

”Ohjelmisto-osaaminen on avainasemassa sen varmistamisessa, että digitaalinen kehitys todella sujuvoittaa arkea ja työntekoa. Vibe-koodaamisella on paikkansa, mutta kun tekoälyllä syntyy palveluita hetkessä, osaavan suunnittelun, määrittelyn ja testaamisen merkitys vain kasvaa. Esimerkiksi tietoturvan taso ei välttämättä näy käyttäjälle, mutta jos se on puutteellinen, seuraukset voivat olla vakavia”, Raesmaa taustoittaa.

Vuoden Digipalvelu -palkintotilaisuudessa julkistetaan myös jo 25. kerran Vuoden Ohjelmistoyrittäjä. Arvostettu tunnustus juhlistaa suomalaisen ohjelmistoteollisuuden kasvua edistänyttä ja toimialaa omalla esimerkillään inspiroinutta yrittäjää.

Vuoden Digipalvelu 2026 -tuomariston jäsenet ovat Riitta Raesmaa, Kamoon Digital (puheenjohtaja); Cristina Andersson, Develor Productions Oy; Kalle Heinonen, AI Finland; Jukka Holm, Visma; Sonja Hyrynsalmi, LUT; Tarja Jernström, Microsoft; Ira Keskitalo, Context& Finland; Mette Kontio, Terveyskylä; Janne Lindfors, Barona; Toni Ranta, IBM ja Katja Vakula, Hion Digital.

title: Outgoing UN chief says polluters have treated atmosphere like an ‘open sewer’
content:
António Guterres laments world leaders’ inaction and says oil and gas firms ‘must pay’ for climate devastation

For one last time, António Guterres tried to fix the world’s gaze upon the dangerously escalating climate crisis. But the departing UN secretary general found world leaders still largely focused on other issues, even after a painful summer of stunning climate-driven disasters.

Speaking to assembled dignitaries at the UN on Tuesday, Guterres railed against big oil for treating “the atmosphere as an open sewer” and warned again of the catastrophic effects of the climate crisis.

title: Webinar Event - Forests for Future: Halting Biodiversity Decline by Restoring Forest Ecosystems
content: Join us on Zoom on November 4, 2026 at 15:00 CEST for the second joint EXTRA/EXALT symposium in collaboration with the TreesForDev research project. Forests are at the front lines of the global climate crisis. In this symposium we explore the still much neglected issue of biodiversity loss and deforestation, sometimes also glossed as ecosystem collapse. Our point of departure is a new pivotal report released by IPBES, the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Biodiversity and Environmental Services, highlighting the economic risks of failing to act on the already dramatic loss of ecosystem health that has been documented. In this symposium we explore the role of afforestation in mitigating biodiversity loss and ecosystem restoration, and in reducing climate change through carbon abatement. We bring together three experts to talk about deforestation, the role of wildfires, afforestation, and how ecological restoration requires more than just tree planting. Our speakers come from the critical social sciences, management and organization studies, and forest policy. Their unique perspectives will support a rich dialogue on what policies will best serve to prevent further forest and biodiversity loss.

title: Türkiye’s crackdown on LGBTI groups and activists is part of an escalating rights crisis
content:
On 13 September, I woke in southwest Türkiye to news of a large-scale operation targeting LGBTI organizations and human rights defenders across the country. Since then, police have arrested at least 116 people across 15 provinces following raids on homes, venues and the offices of LGBTI rights organizations. At least 83 people have been placed in pretrial detention and criminal investigations have been launched against more than 160 people. LGBTI rights organisations have reported allegations of intrusive strip searches, insults and humiliation as well as HRDs being held in isolation in violation of their rights. Hundreds of social media accounts belonging to LGBTI organizations and activists, journalists, media outlets and others have so far been blocked or restricted alongside a number of websites. Those affected include Amnesty International Türkiye’s X account.  

As protest within Türkiye builds and international condemnation mounts, it is clear that the Turkish authorities have every intention of intensifying the crackdown

Milena Buyum, Amnesty International

title: Climate Activists Target AI Data Centers & Amazon's Plan to Build Largest U.S. Gas Power Plant
content:
World leaders are in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, which coincides with Climate Week. It comes after months of climate-fueled extreme weather around the world, including heat waves in North America and Europe, wildfires in Africa, flash flooding in Asia and a record-breaking El Niño.

Climate campaigner Bill McKibben says that while it’s too late to prevent the climate crisis from unfolding, solar and wind energy are now cheap enough “to blunt its worst excesses.”

We also speak with Kavita Sthanumurthy, a former software engineer at Amazon and a member of Amazon Employees for Climate Justice. She says the artificial intelligence boom is largely being powered by dirty fossil fuel, even as companies like Amazon claim they use 100% renewable energy. “We did our own independent research and found that it was closer to 22%,” says Sthanumurthy.

title: Lindtman: ”Hallitus kaahasi ennätystyöllisyydestä EU:n työttömyysykköseksi”
content:
SDP:n puheenjohtaja Antti Lindtman esitteli ensi vuoden budjetin lähetekeskustelussa neljä täsmätoimea, jotka kohdistuvat sinne, missä hintojen nousu tuntuu eniten.

Diesel maksaa jo kaksi ja puoli euroa litralta. Lindtmanin mukaan hallitus on jättänyt ihmiset yksin hintojen noustessa.

– Ennen viime vaaleja moni suomalainen uskoi, että mikäli perussuomalaiset pääsevät hallitukseen, bensan hinta laskee roimasti. Nyt diesel maksaa jo kaksi ja puoli euroa, ja valtiovarainministeri Purra levittelee käsiään. Arvoisa hallitus, ei nyt ihmisiä saa jättää pulaan, Lindtman vetosi.

SDP esittää ensi vuodelle työmatkavähennyksen korottamista, työttömyysturvan ja asumistuen suojaosien palauttamista, kotitalousvähennyksen nostamista ja terveydenhuollon asiakasmaksujen kohtuullistamista.

– Nämä toimet toisivat helpotusta ensi vuodelle. Luottamusta siihen, että tavallinen ihminen selviää. Ja ostovoimaa, jotta yrityksille riittää asiakkaita. Kun ihminen uskaltaa taas käyttää rahaa, kasvu ja työpaikat tulevat kotimarkkinoille.

title: Kuninkaallinen Nukketeatteri saapuu Renkomäen kirjastoon 29.9.
content:
Vuorovaikutteinen lastennäytelmä kutsuu mukaan lorumetsän aakkosjahtiin.


Kirsi Kunnaksen rakastettuihin runoihin perustuvassa Tiitiäisen aakkoset -esityksessä etsitään aakkosia laulujen, lorujen ja pienten pulmien avulla yhdessä yleisön kanssa. Vuorovaikutteinen näytelmä vie pienet katsojat Tiitiäisen metsään, jossa kohdataan mitä merkillisimpiä metsän asukkeja ja löydetään Tiitiäiseltä kadonneita kirjaimia.

Näytelmä pohjautuu Kunnaksen Tiitiäisen tuluskukkaro -runo- ja lorukokoelmaan. Hauskojen ja oivaltavien runojen kautta katsojat tutustuvat aakkosiin. Esitystä rytmittävät myös riemukkaat laulut.

Lavalla nähdään näyttelijä ja taidekasvattaja Taina Maria Savimäki, joka on myös valmistanut esityksen nuket kierrätysmateriaaleista.

Tiitiäisen aakkoset -näytelmä esitetään Renkomäen kirjastossa tiistaina 29.9. klo 18.00.

Esityksen kesto on noin 30 minuuttia. Esitys sopii koko perheelle, erityisesti 2–7-vuotiaille lapsille.

title: Trump rejects global entity for AI oversight
content:
President Donald Trump condemned the idea of a global entity to oversee artificial intelligence in his remarks at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday.

He said the United States “rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control” AI, just a day ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House for meetings, in which AI could be a major topic of discussion.

The president insisted in his remarks that the U.S. is leading the world in AI innovation and reiterated his argument that the technology’s disruptive or possibly dangerous capabilities are a “hoax.” It comes as Trump has warned that efforts to regulate AI could hamper American efforts and allow China to get ahead.

“We’re leading now over China by a lot and everyone else and we’re going to keep it that way. We’re going to keep it very, very straight and very strong. I’m not going to stifle growth of anything that’s going to be bigger than the industrial revolution,” Trump said. “We will be very careful and that’s why we have a Department of Justice.”

The president also said the name should be changed to “super intelligence,” calling on other nations to drop the use of “artificial.”

title: Six-year-old Chinese girl ‘sets new women’s Rubik’s Cube world record’
content:
Lian Yunzhi solves 3x3 puzzle on several occasions in average time of under 4.5 seconds, according to state media

A six-year-old Chinese girl has set a new women’s world record for solving a Rubik’s Cube in just over four seconds, state media reported.

“Speedcuber” Lian Yunzhi broke the women’s 3x3 average world record twice this month at two World Cube Association certified competitions in Wuhan and Guangzhou, according to state broadcaster CCTV on Monday.

title: Väitös: Julkinen vaikuttaminen on moniulotteinen ja merkityksellinen osa sosiaalityötä
content:
Suomalaista sosiaalityötä ja sen tekijöitä on kuvattu tutkimuksissa hiljaiseksi ammattikunnaksi, joka vetäytyy julkisesta keskustelusta. YTM Katriina Sirkan väitöstutkimus osoittaa, että sosiaalityössä vaikuttaminen on aktiivisempaa ja monimuotoisempaa kuin aiemmat tutkimukset antavat ymmärtää.

Suomalaisessa yhteiskunnassa on meneillään lukuisia rakenteellisia muutoksia, jotka haastavat pohtimaan sosiaalityön roolia.

Sosiaalityön toimintaympäristö on viime vuosina muuttunut merkittävästi. Muutokseen ovat vaikuttaneet erityisesti yhteiskunnalliset kehityskulut, kuten globaalit kriisit ja hallinnolliset uudistukset. Sosiaalityön on kyettävä vastaamaan näihin muutoksiin ja uudistumaan, jotta se voi toimia vaikuttavasti.

Katriina Sirkan mukaan suomalaista sosiaalityötä ja sen tekijöitä on kuvattu tutkimuksissa hiljaiseksi ammattikunnaksi, joka vetäytyy julkisesta keskustelusta.

– Hiljaisuuden kulttuurin on esitetty tarkoittavan pelkoa ottaa itsenäisesti kantaa julkisuudessa sosiaalityötä koskeviin kysymyksiin. Tämän seurauksena sosiaalityöntekijät osallistuvat julkiseen keskusteluun usein varovasti tai epäsuorasti, Sirkka kuvailee.

title: Ashfak Mahmud will defend his PhD thesis
content:
Ashfak Mahmud will defend his PhD thesis titled "Multisource remote sensing framework for monitoring soil, crop and land-surface processes in smallholder farms"  on Friday, 2 October 2026, at 12:00 at the University of Helsinki.

This dissertation explores remote sensing approaches for monitoring heterogeneous smallholder agricultural systems in East Africa. The research combines observations from proximal hyperspectral sensors, field cameras, UAVs, and satellites to assess soil organic carbon and nitrogen, monitor crop phenology, biophysical traits and agroclimatic responses, and analyse fractional vegetation cover and land surface temperature. The dissertation demonstrates how observations from different platforms and spatial scales can complement each other to provide more timely, detailed, and scalable information for monitoring diverse smallholder agricultural landscapes.

 The study is one of the results of REACT project (Regenerative agricultural systems for climate resilience in agroecological gradient in East Africa) funded by the Research Council of Finland.

Time: Friday, 2 October 2026, 12:00

title: Purra: Ummehtunut YYA-talouspolitiikka vaihtui tosiasioihin ja tieteeseen
content:
Valtiovarainministeri, perussuomalaisten puheenjohtaja Riikka Purra sanoo hallituksen panostaneen talouspolitiikassaan tosiasioihin, tieteeseen ja uudistamiseen.

Purra avasi eduskunnassa keskustelun valtion ensi vuoden talousarviosta. Hän kuvasi hallituksen veropolitiikkaa historiallisen yrittäjämyönteiseksi, mikä on välttämätöntä talouskasvun vahvistumiseksi.

PURRAN mukaan Suomessa aikaisemmin harjoitettu kymmenien vuosien ajan ”ummehtunutta YYA-talouspolitiikkaa, joka on henkinyt konsensusta, tulonsiirtoja, veromoukaria ja sosiaalivaltion kasvavaa holhoamista”.

– Tarvitsemme toimivia uudistuksia rakenteisiin, hallinnon karsimista ja tuottavuuden nostoa kaikilla toimialoilla, emme vanhan maailman veromoukaria tai hallintohimmelipalapelejä. Ketterä Suomi perustuu korkeaan osaamiseen ja teknologiaan, vahvaan ja ennakoitavaan yrittäjämyönteiseen lainsäädäntöympäristöön sekä kevenevään valtioon, Purra sanoi.

Hallituksen budjettiesitys on 12,4 miljardia alijäämäinen.

Purra myönsi, että julkisen talouden tila on edelleen hyvin vaikea. Hän lisäsi, että esitys on kuitenkin noin miljardin euron verran vähemmän kuin kuluvana vuonna.

title: Pehmojen työpäivä tutustuttaa omat pehmot lähikirjastoon
content:
Mitä kirjastossa tapahtuu silloin, kun pehmot saapuvat kirjastoon töihin ja yökylään? Liipolan kirjasto kutsuu lasten pehmolelut syysretkelle sympaattiseen lähikirjastoon.


Pehmojen työpäivä tarjoaa lapsille mahdollisuuden kurkistaa kirjaston arkeen leikin ja mielikuvituksen kautta sekä tutustua omaan lähikirjastoonsa uudella tavalla.

Pehmojen työpäivä järjestetään torstaina 1.10. Liipolan kirjastossa. Päivän aikana pehmot pääsevät tutustumaan kirjaston tiloihin, seuraamaan kirjaston toimintaa ja osallistumaan erilaisiin työtehtäviin henkilökunnan apuna. Luvassa on tavallisia työpäivän askareita, mutta myös yllätyksiä, joista pehmot voivat kertoa perheilleen kotiin palattuaan.

Työpäivään osallistuvat pehmot tuodaan kirjastoon jo edellisenä iltana. Kirjaston henkilökunta huolehtii pehmoista päivän ajan, ja päivän tapahtumia tallennetaan myös.

title: UK will aim for ‘single set’ of global AI standards at G20
content:
NEW YORK — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Tuesday an international agreement on AI led by the U.K. will seek to establish “a single set of global principles and standards.”

Burnham told a meeting with business leaders in New York that AI will be “the primary focus” of the U.K.’s upcoming G20 presidency.

It comes as discussions about global AI governance have shot up the diplomatic agenda, with Burnham telling journalists on his way to the United Nations General Assembly on Monday that the U.K. could be an “honest broker” for a global agreement on how to approach the technology.

It also came shortly before President Donald Trump used his address to the U.N. to assert that the United States “totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme” to control AI, in contrast to Burnham’s messaging.

“We want to pick up the initiatives that are beginning to emerge, develop, and bring them into a single set of global principles and standards that are very much about unlocking the full potential whilst guarding against the risks,” Burnham told businesses leaders on Tuesday.

title: Big tech says AI can find a cure for cancer. So where is it?
content:
Alongside warnings about its ability to destroy humanity, artificial intelligence is also hailed for its potential to revolutionise health treatment. Just how far can it take us?

Her name was June. June would be the last month she ever knew.

I remember the way her bed made her so small, swallowed her up in the middle of the room, turned as it was to face the window. With her liver failing, her skin was a ghostly apricot. June – I called her Nan – had been stalked by the king of terrors, the emperor of all maladies: cancer. That son of a bitch.

title: Antti Autio will defend his PhD thesis
content:
Antti Autio will defend his PhD thesis titled "Contextuality and Climate Change Adaptation in Taita Taveta County, Kenya: Negotiating Adaptation across Heterogeneous Agroecological Landscapes"  on Friday, 25 September 2026, at 12:00 at the University of Helsinki. 

This dissertation examines climate change adaptation among smallholder farmers in Taita Taveta County, Kenya, through three empirical studies on climate-smart agriculture, contextual vulnerability, regenerative agriculture, and positive deviance. It explores how adaptation is shaped by agroecological diversity, institutions, markets, gendered vulnerabilities, local knowledge, and farmer agency. The dissertation argues that adaptation is not simply the adoption of externally promoted practices or technologies, but a contextual, negotiated, and relational process emerging from everyday farming decisions within heterogeneous agroecological landscapes. 

Time: Friday, 25 September 2026, 12:00–
Venue: Athena, Hall 302, Siltavuorenpenger 3, Helsinki

title: Pakistan: Arbitrary detention of Imran Khan’s family and party activists a flagrant violation of human rights
content:
Responding to the arbitrary detention of members of former prime minister Imran Khan’s family, including his three sisters, as well as activists from Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party’s planned protests and march on 27 September , Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for South Asia, said: 

“The targeting of Imran Khan’s family and PTI party activists is a flagrant violation of their rights to liberty, freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly. Such actions speak to the severity of the current restrictions in Pakistan. 

“The pre-emptive arrests of PTI members come ahead of planned country-wide protests by the party on 27 September, which government officials have openly vowed to stop. Roadblocks are already being erected in Islamabad. These developments do not bode well, especially given the authorities’ long track record of reckless and unlawful use of force against protesters. A protest cannot be deemed violent before it has even started. Pakistan’s authorities must uphold their obligations under international human rights law to facilitate peaceful assembly and refrain from unlawful measures to thwart these protests.

title: Analysis: ‘Super El Niño’ reaches ‘remarkable’ all-time record
content:
This year’s so-called “super El Niño” is entering into record-breaking territory. 

Sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific now equal the previous daily record set in 2015 and will likely keep rising in the days ahead.

El Niño is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon in the Pacific that reshapes weather patterns around the world and temporarily boosts global temperatures. 

The current El Niño event – which has been underway since June and is expected to last until next year – has been developing faster than any previous event on record. 

The strength of an event is tracked using the “Niño 3.4 anomaly”, which measures how much warmer sea surface temperatures in a section of the central Pacific are than average. 

As of 19 September, the daily anomaly in the Niño 3.4 region stands at 3.07C, putting it in a statistical tie with the previous record of 3.08C.

Some scientists, using a different baseline for calculating the anomaly, have already called the new record. 

Either way, this is remarkable, in part because of how early in the calendar year it is occurring. El Niño typically peaks in the winter months, most commonly in November or December.

title: Burden-EU: understanding the burden of disease
content:
Every breath we take contains tiny particles that are invisible to the naked eye and can harm our health. Air pollution alone contributes to heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, and other chronic illnesses. But how can we measure its real impact on people’s lives? How does it compare with other threats, such as smoking, diabetes or infectious diseases?

To answer these questions, scientists use a measure called the Disability-Adjusted Life Year (DALY). This combines years of life lost due to premature death with years lived with illness, showing how much of a population’s health is lost to specific diseases and risk factors. This helps governments to see the bigger picture and decide where to invest for the greatest health gains.

Before the launch of the COST Action European Burden of Disease Network (Burden-EU), each country used different methods, making comparisons almost impossible. The COST Action brought together almost 500 researchers from over 60 countries to create a shared framework for carrying out these studies. The result is more reliable, comparable data to inform policies that can save lives.

title: A Principled Approach as the Sands Shift
content:
Creative Commons has been exploring questions around artificial intelligence for a long time: how this profound technological shift might affect people’s motivations to share, whether the intentions behind sharing work before AI became mainstream still hold when we consider how those works are being used now, and how we sustain a thriving commons when the fundamental bargain of the open web has shifted.

Throughout these changes, we have been guided by a commitment to balance creator agency in how people participate in the commons, while preserving the public’s right to reuse. CC licenses operate through copyright, and in many jurisdictions, copyright exceptions and limitations may permit certain AI development and training uses. That can leave people who want to share openly with limited ways to impose conditions, leading some to resort to restricting access instead. This risks pushing us towards an all-or-nothing binary between a free-for-all or enclosure. We fear the end result will be a retracted knowledge commons.

So we’ve been revisiting some fundamental questions:

  • When are norms enough, and when are enforceable conditions needed?

title: Agiatis Benardou Delivers Keynote and Receives IEEE Award
content:
Agiatis Benardou, President of the Board of Directors of DARIAH, delivered a keynote address at the 2nd IEEE International Conference on Cyber Humanities (IEEE CH 2026), held in Venice, Italy, from 7 to 9 September 2026. The conference brought together researchers, practitioners and representatives of Research Infrastructures working across the intersection of digital technologies, the Social Sciences and Humanities, and cultural heritage.

On 8 September, Benardou delivered her keynote, “From User Needs to Knowledge Ecosystems: Designing Human-Centred Infrastructures for Digital Cultural Heritage”. Drawing on her experience across European digital cultural heritage initiatives and Research Infrastructures, she explored how the field is moving from individual digital tools and platforms towards interconnected knowledge ecosystems. Her central argument was that the challenge is no longer simply to build technically sophisticated systems, but to create infrastructures that become meaningfully embedded in the ways researchers and cultural heritage professionals work, collaborate and produce knowledge.

title: "America, Who Hurt You?": Tony-Winning Performer Sarah Jones on New NY Solo Show & Art as Resistance
content:
Sarah Jones has been described as “a one-woman global village” for her remarkable one-person, multi-character shows. The Tony- and Obie Award-winning writer and performer is best known for her Broadway hit Bridge and Tunnel. She is back in New York with her latest solo performance, America, Who Hurt You?, which is being presented by the National Black Theatre and the Theatre for a New Audience at Polonsky Shakespeare Center in Brooklyn.

America, Who Hurt You? “starts with our history of genocide as a country, our history of enslaving African people, our history of indentured servitude,” says Jones. “This show … is about restoring the history that has intentionally been erased.”

Häkkänen teki kuun puolivälissä Israeliin työvierailun, josta kerrottiin vasta jälkeenpäin. Matkalla Häkkänen tapasi Israelin puolustusministerin Israel Katzin ja muita poliittisia vaikuttajia sekä vieraili Libanonissa suomalaisten rauhanturvaajien luona.

Etenkin Katzin kanssa asioiminen on suututtanut oppositiota. Katz on ilmoittanut, että Israel aikoo yhä tyhjentää miehittämänsä Gazan alueen asukkaista ja pakkosiirtää noin kaksi miljoonaa ihmistä muualle.

Toteutuessaan teko olisi sotarikos.

VIIKONLOPPUNA muassa vihreiden puheenjohtaja Sofia Virta kritisoi Häkkäsen toimintaa ja kertoi aikovansa esittää epäluottamusta puolustusministerille. Vasemmistoliitto on ilmoittanut tukevansa vihreitä tässä.

Virran mielestä Suomen pitäisi painostaa Israelia lopettamaan sotatoimensa Gazassa, eikä antaa Katzille virallisen ministerivierailun kaltaisia tuenosoituksia.

Sofia Virta vetosi maanantaina demareihin, että nämä tulisivat mukaan Häkkäs-epäluottamuslauseeseen.

title: Wiki Rookies: Daejeon in-person meetup
content:
From late July to early August, roads across Korea are traditionally packed with people heading off on vacation.

In early August, the Wikimedia community in Korea and neurodivergent participants also took a special kind of vacation of their own: a photowalk in Yeongwol.

Yeongwol is well known for its historic sites associated with King Danjong, as well as for the film The Man Who Lives with the King, which tells a story centered on him.

We’d like to invite you, our readers, to join us as we look back on our time there.

The day of our photowalk, August 1, fell during what was close to the peak of Korea’s summer heatwave.

Since most of our route involved outdoor activities, we first filled up on some refreshing makguksu before heading out.

The tangy flavors of Seoul-style makguksu, the rich meaty broth of Gyeongsang-style milmyeon, and the mild, delicate taste of Gangwon-style makguksu came together to create a whole new world of flavors: Yeongwol-style makguksu.

Our next stop was Cheongnyeongpo, the first place where Danjong was exiled after being demoted to the status of Nosangun.

title: Red flags at the start of Apple’s John Ternus era
content:
Tim Cook isn’t the “main character” at Apple anymore. During the company’s keynote presentation on September 9, the long-serving CEO publicly passed the torch to his successor, former hardware engineering lead John Ternus, in time to be the face of a raft of new hardware announcements. There were new Apple Watches, AirPods, iPhones, and, most important of all, the long-expected folding iPhone Duo.

As the announcements progressed, many were watching not just to see what new electronics were coming from one of the mostly highly valued companies on the planet, but also how that company might change under the direction of a new leader. Would Ternus be a continuation of the Cook approach to management? Would new hardware make a comeback after years of tweaks and revenue maximization? Would Apple finally go harder on generative AI after taking a slower and more measured approach to rolling out such features?

title: D.C. Circuit Must Vacate a Drone Flight Restriction That Criminalized Recording Immigration Agents
content:
EFF joined an amicus brief with ACLU, ACLU of D.C., National Press Photographers Association, and Professional Photographers of America to urge the D.C. Circuit to vacate an FAA drone flight restriction that violated the First Amendment right to record law enforcement. This is an important case—Levine v. FAA—challenging the ability of the government to punish drone pilots who record law enforcement officers engaged in official business. 

As we wrote about earlier this year, the FAA issued a flight restriction for drones that had effectively criminalized the recording of Department of Homeland Security officers, including immigration agents from ICE and CBP, and their vehicles (what the FAA called “mobile assets” including “ground vehicle convoys and their associated escorts”) even if the drone was over half a mile away. 

A drone operator, represented by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, sued the FAA in March [PDF]. But in April, the FAA rescinded the flight restriction.

content:

title: Russia’s Baltic escalation playbook: fear is part of the strategy
content:
Russia is promoting a picture of the Baltic region in which NATO is preparing to attack Russia, Baltic governments are heavily militarising, and Russian speakers face imminent persecution. Taken together, these narratives create an atmosphere of permanent crisis in which military escalation appears increasingly plausible. This allows Moscow to exert pressure even without taking overt military action – the possibility of conflict itself becomes an instrument of coercion.

In late 2025, the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) drew attention to the steady stream of Russian FIMI targeting the Baltic countries, noting that they mirror the narratives that the Kremlin used to try to justify its invasions of Ukraine. Recent Baltic intelligence assessments describe a sustained and increasingly organised Russian effort to influence the information environment in Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia, disseminating anti-Baltic narratives through social media and coordinated cross-platform campaigns.

title: Two Years Ago, Meta Killed CrowdTangle. Can a New AI Tool Fill the Void?
content:
In 2024, Meta shuttered CrowdTangle, a tool used to track how content spread across Facebook and Instagram. The portal was an essential tool for journalists, fact-checkers, and researchers, who used it for more than a decade to monitor viral content — and the spread of misinformation.

CrowdTangle’s end came slowly. Meta disinvested in the tool over years by cutting funding, disbanding teams, and restricting users. When the company finally announced in March 2024 that CrowdTangle would cease operations in August, a petition signed by more than 100 social media watchdog groups and others warned that, as a result, “almost all outside efforts to identify and prevent political disinformation, incitements to violence, and online harassment of women and minorities will be silenced.”

title: Political Prisoner Ali Zarei, Sentenced to Death, Transferred to Solitary Confinement
content:
According to HRANA, political prisoner Ali Zarei Douzdarresi has been transferred to solitary confinement.

The transfer of this political prisoner from Ward 37 of Unit 3 at Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj to solitary confinement took place today, Monday, September 21.

As of the time of this report, no further details have been obtained regarding the reason for Mr. Zarei Douzdarresi’s transfer to solitary confinement.

He recently announced in an audio message from Ghezel Hesar Prison, which was circulated on social media, that his death sentence had been upheld.

Earlier this month, Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced this political prisoner to death on the charge of “corruption on earth through extensive involvement in political activities, creating the appearance of fabricated damages, producing false reports, propaganda against the regime, disrupting security, and illegally entering and leaving the country.”

title: Bhutan Should Release All Remaining Political Prisoners
content:
When Bhutan’s Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay meets world leaders at the United Nations general assembly in New York this week, they should urge him to release the at least 28 political prisoners who are still held in dreadful conditions in his country’s jails.

The small Himalayan kingdom projects itself to the world as the land that invented “gross national happiness,” but that image is belied by its detention and treatment of political prisoners.

Most are from the country’s Nepali-speaking community, and their cases relate to a period of rights violations that the community faced in the early 1990s. They were allegedly tortured before being convicted of terrorism and treason offenses at trials during which they had no defense lawyers. Most are serving sentences of life without parole.

Four of the prisoners belong to the Sharchop ethnic community and were accused of membership of the Druk National Congress, a banned political party that existed before Bhutan introduced democratic reforms in 2008.

title: Antti Aaltonen: Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle -avaus
content:
Erityisasiantuntija Antti Aaltonen Opetushallituksen Lukutaito-ohjelmasta avaa kolmiosaisen ”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -koulutuskokonaisuuden ensimmäisen tilaisuuden.

Tallenne on ”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -webinaarista, joka järjestettiin 16.9.2026 osana lasten ja nuorten lukutaitotyön koulutuskokonaisuutta. Tilaisuus oli suunnattu peruskoulun opettajille ja kirjastohenkilöstölle, mutta oli avoin kaikille aiheesta kiinnostuneille. Avauksessaan Aaltonen esittelee päivän ohjelman ja taustoittaa sitä kansallisella lukutaitostrategialla (2021–2030) ja sen kolmella suuntaviivalla, keskittyen erityisesti lukemaan innostamisen teemaan. Lopuksi hän nostaa esiin Suomen Sanataideopetuksen Seuran Hehkuvat sanat -kyselyn (2024–2025) tuloksia siitä, mitä lapset ja nuoret itse toivovat lukemiselta.

”Oikea kirja oikealle lukijalle” -webinaarin järjestivät yhteistyössä Seinäjoen kaupunginkirjaston valtakunnallinen erityistehtävä (SJK Erte), Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, Tampereen, Lahden ja Vaasan alueellista kehittämistehtävää hoitavat kirjastot sekä Opetushallituksen Lukutaito-ohjelman Lukeva koulu -toiminta. ”Fuck the politicians: jos he eivät kuuntele, niin ei sitten. Lähdetään itse tekemään tätä hommaa.” 

Se on viesti, jonka opiskelija, ilmastoaktivisti ja elokuvantekijä Hanna Höijer, 22, haluaa sukupolvelleen välittää. 

Hän on kyllästynyt siihen, että nuorille tarjotaan lääkkeeksi ilmastoahdistukseen lähes pelkästään protestointia, vaatimusten esittämistä päättäjille tai somessa toimimista. Periaatteessa se on hyvä asia, mutta samalla herkästi myös vähätellään nuorten omia kykyjä ja jätetään heidät muiden armoille, hän sanoo. 

Höijer näkee, että ihmiset jaetaan julkisessa keskustelussa ilmastonmuutoksen uhreihin ja ratkaisijoihin. Uhreja ovat nuoret, ratkaisijoita taas yleensä ”keski-ikäiset valkoiset eurooppalaiset miehet puvuissa.” 

”Tämä jaottelu häiritsee minua. Joo, nuoret ovat uhreja, mutta se ei tarkoita, etteivätkö nuoret voisi olla myös ratkaisijoita.” 

Siksi hän tekee kollegoineen parhaillaan dokumenttielokuvaa Not Done Yet, joka tuo parrasvaloihin ilmastonmuutokseen konkreettisia ratkaisuja Afrikassa kehittävät nuoret.

title: When Galileo Calculated the Precise Dimensions of Hell in Dante’s Inferno
content:
We venerate Galileo Galilei for daring to speak the scientific truth in the face of severe institutional opposition. He publicly acknowledged that the Earth revolves around the Sun in a time when the Church would rather he didn’t, displaying a bloody-mindedness that he seems to have acquired with age. Decades earlier, in the first stage of his career, he found himself (circa 1588) tasked by the Florentine Academy with calculating the precise dimensions of hell as described in Dante’s Divine Comedy. Dutifully applying himself to this now-absurd-sounding work, he determined that the underworld’s roof had to be centered in Jerusalem, as wide as the radius of the entire Earth, and no less than 600 kilometers thick.

Not that any of this was based on frivolous reasoning. As a model for the dimensions of hell’s roof, for instance, Galileo looked over to Filippo Brunelleschi’s dome, which had topped the Florence Cathedral for a century and a half at that point. Galileo’s calculations of hell’s dimensions contradicted an earlier model proposed by the scholar Alessandro Vellutello. Instead, they supported a model developed by architect Antonio Manetti, whose drawings appear here.

title: Presidentti Stubb ja Norjan pääministeri: Tekoälyn nopea kehitys vaatii kansainvälistä yhteistyötä
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb ja Norjan pääministeri Jonas Gahr Støre ovat tehneet kansainvälisen vetoomuksen, jonka tavoitteena on varmistaa, että kaikkein kehittyneimmät tekoälymallit pysyvät edelleen ihmiskunnan hallinnassa.

Tähän mennessä vetoomukseen on liittynyt 22 johtajaa 20 maasta eri puolilta maailmaa. Vetoomuksessa ovat sen julkistushetkellä mukana Suomen presidentin ja pääministerin sekä Norjan pääministerin lisäksi Tanskan, Islannin, Viron, Latvian, Alankomaiden, Irlannin, Euroopan komission, Saksan, Espanjan, Moldovan, Turkin, Yhdistyneiden Arabiemiraattien, Bahrainin, Kazakstanin, Singaporen, Kenian, Etelä-Afrikan, Kanadan ja Australian johtajat. Stubb ja Støre kannustavat myös muita maita liittymään vetoomukseen.

Tekoäly on ihmiskunnan suurimpia teknologisia muutoksia. Se tulee vaikuttamaan politiikkaan, talouteen, turvallisuuteen, tieteeseen ja ihmisyyteen. Ihmisten tulee olla kuljettajan paikalla tässä muutoksessa. Meillä on vaihtoehtoja tekoälyn kanssa toimimiseen: voimme kilpailla, tehdä yhteistyötä tai vetäytyä. Oikea vaihtoehto on tehdä yhteistyötä, presidentti Stubb sanoo.

title: Watch: The New Supreme Court
content:
The Supreme Court continues to make consequential rulings in the shadows. I analyzed tens of thousands of case files from the court’s online archives, parsing through filings to separate simple requests for deadline extensions from challenges to long-established constitutional rights. I discovered that in the term that ended in 2025, the justices issued more substantive decisions on their emergency docket than in cases argued in open court. Experts told me this was likely the first time this has happened in the court’s modern history. 

Representatives from the Supreme Court did not respond to my questions. 

Since I reported that story in July, more major rulings have been made on the emergency docket, often called the “shadow docket,” where justices rarely hear arguments and often issue unsigned orders that don’t explain how they arrived at their decisions or even how they voted.

title: Usein kysyttyä: Lainauskorvauksen kuvavähennys
content:
Kuvavähennys on Sanaston työkalu lainauskorvausten tasapuoliseen jakamiseen. Kuvavähennyksen avulla suunnataan suurempi osuus Sanaston lainauskorvauksesta tekstipainotteisten teosten tekijöille.

Käytännössä runsaammin kuvia sisältävien kirjastoluokkien teoksista maksetaan pienempi lainauskorvaus tekstintekijälle. Korvausten laskentaan käytetään kirjastoluokkakohtaista kuvavähennyskerrointa. Lisäksi tänä vuonna Sanasto pilotoi runouden kirjastoluokassa tarkempaa teoskohtaista kuvavähennystä.

Jos kuvavähennyksiä ei tehtäisi, olisi lainakohtainen korvaus kaikille teoslainoille alhaisempi kirjastoluokasta riippumatta, koska Sanasto jakaa kiinteää määrärahaa lainojen kesken.

Kuvavähennys toimii niin, että yli 10 % kuvaa sisältävissä kirjastoluokissa on kerroin, joka huomioi kuvan osuuden teoksessa. Kuvien keskimääräinen osuus eri kirjastoluokkien teoksissa on selvitetty käymällä läpi kattava otanta ko. kirjastoluokan teoksia. Esimerkiksi kertomakirjallisuudesta tekstintekijä saa 100 % lainauskorvauksesta ja sarjakuvista tekstintekijä saa 37,5 % lainauskorvauksesta. Tilitysjärjestelmämme tekee kuvavähennyksen automaattisesti teoksille niiden kirjastoluokan mukaan.

title: Kirjastojen tietoturvaa pitää tukea
content:
Viime viikolla Suomessa uutisoitiin laajasti kirjastojen tietojärjestelmiin kohdistuneesta palvelunestohyökkäyksestä.

Hyökkäykset johtuvat siitä, että kirjastot ovat tärkeä osa kriittistä infrastruktuuria. Ne tarjoavat kaikille avoimen pääsyn tietoon, digitaalisiin palveluihin, kulttuuriin ja oppimiseen. Ne ovat yksi harvoista julkisista palveluista, jotka ovat aidosti kaikkien saavutettavissa asuinpaikasta, varallisuudesta tai taustasta riippumatta.

Asiakkaiden tiedot eivät ilmeisesti ole vaarantuneet, mutta hyökkäys on muistutus siitä, että kirjastojen toimintaan kohdistuu vihamielistä mielenkiintoa.

Kirjastojen tietojärjestelmiin kohdistuvat hyökkäykset ovat erityisen haitallisia, sillä niiden vaikutukset kohdistuvat suoraan kansalaisiin ja heidän mahdollisuuksiinsa saada tietoa ja osallistua yhteiskunnan toimintaan.

Näiden hyökkäysten pitää herätellä päättäjiä siihen, että osana yhteiskunnan tietohuollon kokonaisturvallisuutta kirjastot tarvitsevat kunnolliset resurssit myös tietoturvan ylläpitoon ja kehittämiseen.

title: Sveriges Museer på Bokmässan – om konstens frihet och samtidens uttryck
content:
Foto: Niklas Maupoix

På torsdag finns Sveriges Museer på Bokmässan i Göteborg med två seminarier som på olika sätt tar sig an konstens roll och villkor i vår tid.

Sveriges Museer har i projektet Samtidskonsten sporrar lyft utmaningar och möjligheter för museer att arbeta med samtidskonst. Satsningen har visat att samtidskonsten och dess aktörer ofta fungerar som inspiratörer och utmanar traditionella arbetssätt. Men hur förhåller sig vår tids konstnärliga uttryck till dem inom skönlitteraturen och dramatiken – vad förenar och skiljer dem åt? Deltagare: Gunnar Ardelius, samtalsledare, generalsekretare och författare, Linda Zachrison, konstnärlig chef på Göteborgs stadsteater, Maria Lind, useichef KIN, Kiruna museum för samtidskonst, och Jonathan Brott, poet och redaktör L’Amour – La Mort.

title: EU lawmakers float product liability rules to help avert AI disaster
content:
BRUSSELS — European lawmakers are pushing to expand the EU’s flagship AI regulations to hold American tech companies liable for the risks their most advanced models pose to humanity, according to correspondence seen by POLITICO.

The proposal by four senior lawmakers in the European Parliament would add new rules to the EU’s landmark 2024 AI Act to ensure that companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic could be held liable when their technology is deployed in unforeseen ways.

The move shows Brussels is waking up to a reality in which AI-powered harm is already happening, and risks are multiplying — and marks the first concrete effort within the EU to respond to fears over AI safety that are dominating the global political agenda.

The group is calling on the Commission to introduce an AI Liability Act “to fill the legislative gaps currently existing for these kinds of incidents, so no people or European businesses are left empty-handed against these big providers when they cause harm,” according to a Sept. 16 note to the Commission seen by POLITICO.

Their complaints form the basis of a lawsuit brought against the Elon Musk-owned electric car company by the state of California, which began trial with opening statements on Monday.

title: From French outpost to Euro-Canadian corridor? Why Carney and Macron met in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not need to cross the Atlantic to meet Emmanuel Macron on French soil over the weekend. Instead, he joined the French president in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, just 25 kilometres off Newfoundland.

It was the first official visit to the archipelago by a Canadian prime minister.

The visit brought together a contentious shared history, Canada’s rapprochement with Europe and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon’s search for new development opportunities.

Covering 242 square kilometres and home to around 6,000 people, the archipelago rarely attracts international attention. Yet its location gave the weekend meeting particular significance as France and Canada seek closer ties amid growing tensions with the United States.

After repeatedly threatening to make Canada a 51st state, U.S. President Donald Trump recently posted a map depicting an expanded U.S. encompassing Canada, Greenland and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.

Evidence of Indigenous presence in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon dates back nearly 5,000 years. It later attracted European explorers, including Frenchman Jacques Cartier in 1536.

title: Three Ts will dominate Trump-Xi summit – but expect little movement on trade, less on Taiwan and who knows on tech
content:
When Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping last sat down in May 2026, talk was centered on three Ts: trade, technology and Taiwan.

The latest summit, due to begin in the United States on Sept. 24, looks set to focus on the same set of issues again. The main difference will be that the technology element has been given added urgency by the sudden and rapid shift in developments in artificial intelligence.

What’s less clear is whether the two sides will be able to come to any sort of transformative agreement on that, or any other issue.

The most urgent issue, but also the simplest to solve, will be on trade.

Nearly a year ago at Busan in South Korea, Trump and Xi hammered out an agreement whereby the U.S. agreed to lift some export controls on high-end technology and to reduce the then three-figure tariffs on Chinese goods. For its part, China agreed not to restrict the flow of critical minerals and rare earths to U.S. users.

That pact is now up for renewal. Both sides are likely to want a continuation of the current arrangement, and while there may be some tweaking on the side, the new deal will probably be similar to the old one.
snippet: When Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping last sat down in May 2026, talk was centered on three Ts: trade, technology and Taiwan.

title: Op-ed | Conflict Prevention Has Never Been More Important
content:
To mark the International Day of Peace (21 September), Alex Ballinger MP and Alastair Carr draw on Peace Works – a new report from a coalition of peacebuilding organisations – to argue that a more dangerous world requires the UK to protect the capacity to prevent conflict as well as respond to it.

In July 2011, the UK Government published its Building Stability Overseas Strategy, outlining three guiding principles for conflict prevention: early warning, rapid response and upstream prevention.[1]

Fifteen years on, these principles endure, but the world they were written for is gone. The institutions and assumptions of the liberal international order have weakened and fragmented, replaced by unilateralism, ad hoc alliances, and the arbitrary exercise of hard power.

title: Joshua Farinella on his whistleblowing journey
content:
Joshua Farinella shares his whistleblowing journey, looking back at what happened after he came forward with evidence of food safety, human rights, and labor abuses at a shrimp processing factory in India. With his permission, we’re sharing his words here.

Sometimes you don’t see the impact of whistleblowing until you step back and look at the timeline.

A few years ago, I came forward with evidence about serious problems I had witnessed in the international shrimp supply chain—including forced labor, food-safety concerns, and potential trade violations.

Here’s what happened next:

🔹 2023–2024 — I provided thousands of documents, emails, WhatsApp messages, videos, recordings and other evidence concerning conditions and practices I had witnessed.

🔹 March 2024 — Members of Congress formally sought the underlying evidence and began pursuing the allegations through congressional oversight.

🔹 April 2024 — My whistleblower allegations were raised directly with the FDA Commissioner during a congressional hearing.

🔹 May 2024 — The FDA subsequently took action involving imported shrimp from the facility at issue.

title: Kalatalousalalle tarvitaan uusia osaajia – Turun AMK käynnistää uuden koulutuspolun
content:
Turun ammattikorkeakoulussa käynnistyy syksyllä 2026 uusi kalatalousalan ammattilaisille suunnattu kalan jalostusketjun ja tuotekehityksen koulutuspolku. Koulutus vastaa alan osaajatarpeeseen tilanteessa, jossa kalatalousala uudistuu ja tarvitsee uudenlaista osaamista. Vastaavaa AMK-tasoista koulutusta ei tällä hetkellä ole tarjolla Suomessa.

Kalatalousala on murroksessa. Kotimaisen kalan käyttöä pyritään lisäämään samalla kun kilpailukykyä haastavat kalan tuonti ulkomailta, uusien alalle tulijoiden vähyys ja koulutettujen osaajien puute.

Kehitys kalatalousalla edellyttää nykyaikaisia kalankasvatus- ja jalostusmenetelmiä, automaatiota ja ennen kaikkea laatua, vastuullisuutta ja kuluttajakysyntää tukevia toimintatapoja. Eläköitymisen takia alalta poistuu lähivuosina huomattava määrä työntekijöitä. Alalla tarvitaan osaajia, jotka tuntevat sekä laatuasiat että jalostusprosessin ja kalakaupan vaatimukset.

title: The American Folklife Center Turns 50: See the New Exhibit
content:
—This is a guest post by Stephen Winik, a folklorist in the American Folklife Center. It also appears in the September/October issue of the Library of Congress Magazine.

The American Folklife Center turns 50 in 2026, marking a half century of preserving, presenting and supporting folk culture. The celebration culminates in mid-September with the opening of a major exhibition, “Alive in Many Hands: The American Folklife Center at 50.”

The center owes its existence to the American Folklife Preservation Act of 1976. Congress charged it with safeguarding the nation’s living cultural traditions — everything from fiddle tunes and quilt patterns to holiday rituals, occupational skills and family recipes. These expressions belong to families, ethnic communities, work groups, religious congregations and regions, stretching from the mainland to the Caribbean and Pacific Islands.

Today, the center maintains one of the largest folklife archives anywhere. It exchanges knowledge and expertise with scholars and communities and produces public programs that bring these traditions to life.

title: Kapsäkissa hatut viuhuvat ja roolit vaihtuvat
content:
Tuulikki Närhinsalo 

Kapsäkin uutuus vie 1400-luvun puoliväliin, Schlimmer-nimiseen saksalaiseen pikkukaupunkiin, mutta vain osaksi, sillä musikaalissa ollaan myös omassa ajassamme. Amerikkalaiskaverukset Doug ja Bud ideoivat ja kehittelevät käsikirjoitusta ja musiikkia Johannes Gutenbergistä kertovaan minimusikaaliin, jolle he toivovat menestystä Broadwaylla.

Anthony Kingin ja Scott Brownin käsikirjoittama ja säveltämä vauhdikas minimusikaali poukkoilee taitavasti Gutenberg-tarinan sekä Dougin – Joel Mäkinen ja Budin – Juha Pulli hyvin nykyaikaisen ajatusmaailman välillä. Siinä on niin aitoa hetkessä improvisoinnin ja keksinnän tuntua, että välillä melkein unohtuu, että jokainen repliikki on peräisin amerikkalaisesta käsikirjoituksesta.

title: AI Safety – Little Hope for a US-China Deal
content:
Concerns over AI safety are growing, fueled by a series of autonomous agent breakouts and fears that humanity is on the verge of losing control to superintelligent AI swarms.

Amodei also warned that Chinese dominance could present national security risks, provoking Chinese state media to denounce a “Cold War playbook.” But President Donald ⁠Trump has brushed aside ​calls to slow AI development, saying that “very negative forces” exaggerated concerns. Expect any agreement to be narrowly scoped. 

CEPA fellows see little progress emerging from the upcoming US-China summit in Washington.

title: Is this how the world ends? Extinction scenarios are taking over the AI debate.
content:
Aya Ibrahim, who leads national security work for the AI Now Institute, an independent research organization, said that any limitations of AI predictions may get little scrutiny from elected officials. Policymakers have a track record of being deferential when dealing with the tech sector, she said.

“When it comes to tech issues, there’s just this culture of learned helplessness from the same policymakers that sit on energy and commerce [committees] and oversee the FDA and prescription drugs,” topics where they don’t question their right to govern, said Ibrahim, a former Biden White House official. “Suddenly, if you can’t code the model yourself, then you’re not in a position to weigh in.”

title: "Extraordinary Rendition All Over Again": U.S. Deportees Sent to Equatorial Guinea Beaten, Imprisoned
content:
Two men deported from the United States to Equatorial Guinea were arrested by local police forces and transferred to a prison earlier this month, in apparent retaliation for speaking out about conditions they faced in the Central African country. Samson Birhane, who is from Eritrea, and Ahmed Soliman, a gay asylum seeker from Egypt, were both deported by the Trump administration despite U.S. immigration courts granting them protections.

On September 11, police forces arrived at Hotel Bamy in the city of Malabo, where more than two dozen people have been confined after their deportation from the United States to Equatorial Guinea, a country they have no ties to, as part of President Trump’s secretive “third-country” agreements. Birhane and Soliman say they were arrested and taken to prison for speaking out about the inhumane conditions endured by U.S. deportees at the hotel and threats by armed forces. While confined at the hotel, U.S. deportees have decried denial of medical care and legal assistance, and abuses they’ve described as psychological torture.

title: Eight new ECCCH Sister Projects start
content:
Following the Call for Innovative Use Cases for the Cultural Heritage Cloud (HORIZON-CL2-2025-01-HERITAGE-03), ECHOES is delighted to welcome eight more Sister Projects.

CULTUR-ACT – Collaborative Use Case Living Labs Fostering Tools and ResoURces Validation and Adoption in the European Cloud for Next-Gen Digital Heritage Communities Cooperation

CULTURAL.ACT is designed as a real-world proving ground for the ECCCH, leveraging on a community of CHIs and CCIs – of diverse types, cultural heritage domains, disciplines, size and expertise – that agree to collaborate and share experiences in the use of ECCCH tools and resources in core tasks of their own processes and working environments.

HERITWIN – Cultural Heritage Digital Twins

HERITWIN strengthens Europe’s cultural resilience by validating the European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage (ECCCH) through five real large-scale pilots in Sweden, Norway, Spain, The UK (Northern Ireland), and Greece. The project advances semantic digital twins, eXtended Reality reconstructions, preparedness modelling tools to support conservation, education, public engagement, tourism, and interoperable European data spaces.

title: EU Kids Act Won't Keep the Internet Accountable and Trustworthy
content:
The EU Commission draft law to restrict young people’s access to the internet that it presented last week will come at a high cost: it will put online services behind age gates, expand the use of intrusive age verification, and undermine the privacy of all users. 

The EU Kids Act aims to protect children from risks associated with social media, video games, and AI systems by introducing age-based access rules, safety requirements, and stronger enforcement and oversight measures. It presents itself as building on the Digital Services Act (DSA) and puts into “hard law” some of the safety-by-design measures specified in the non-binding DSA guidelines on minors’ protection. 

The proposal is built around the following elements: social media age “delay”, safety by design, age assurance and parental responsibility, and strong enforcement. Each of these measures are concerning.

title: What deep sea mining could mean for Jamaica’s fisherfolk
content:
‘Any activity that disrupts ocean health could have downstream consequences…’

Originally published on Global Voices

Image of an underwater shot of a vessel with a Jamaican flag on the bottom of its hull, created using Canva Pro elements.

For Jamaica’s fisherfolk, the sea has always been a critical source of food, livelihood, freedom and the future. It’s their pantry, workplace, and cultural centre, but as global companies look to the minerals lying deep below the ocean floor, questions emerge: what will happen to the fishers who rely on these waters when the seabed itself becomes a resource to be exploited?

The way that question is answered could shape the future of Jamaica’s fisheries, and resilience among communities is already bearing the brunt of climate change events. Deep-sea mining may generate sediment plumes, destroy habitats and reduce the biodiversity that cascades through the food chain, placing fisherfolk in the middle of an uncertain ocean economy.

title: Vahideh Haghparast Sentenced to Prison by Mashhad Revolutionary Court
content:
According to HRANA, Vahideh Haghparast has been sentenced to prison.

Under a ruling issued by Branch 1 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, Ms. Haghparast was sentenced to three years and seven months in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion against national security” and nine months on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

An informed source told HRANA that the hearing on the charges against Ms. Haghparast was held on September 1, 2026, in the absence of both her and her defense attorney. The source said that Haghparast was unable to attend the court session due to illness and had filed a formal request to reschedule the hearing.

Haghparast was arrested on December 12, 2025, during the seventh-day memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi in Mashhad. She was released one month later after posting bail.

Vahideh Haghparast, also known as Noura Haghi, holds a doctoral degree in veterinary medicine.

title: Armenian Prisoners in Azerbaijan Allege Rights’ Violations
content:
Ruben Vardanyan, a former senior official in Nagorno-Karabakh's de facto administration who is serving a 20-year prison sentence in Azerbaijan, says that he and 18 other Armenian prisoners are being denied regular family contact, adequate exercise, medical tests, and other rights provided under Azerbaijani law.

In an audio appeal recorded on September 16 and published two days later, Vardanyan addressed Azerbaijan's human rights commissioner, Sabina Aliyeva. He said some prisoners at Umbaki prison do not receive weekly phone calls and none can make video calls. "When my cellmate was arrested, his child was 10 months old," Vardanyan said. "Now the child is more than 3 years old and has not seen his father."

Vardanyan said he has been unable to get medical tests even at his own expense, access notary services, or receive written responses to complaints. He said prisoners get only 20 to 40 minutes of outdoor exercise once a week, rather than an hour a day.

Human Rights Watch has not independently verified these allegations.

On September 19, Aliyeva’s office rejected the allegations that the prisoners’ rights were being violated.

title: Vetoomus kaikkein kehittyneimpien tekoälymallien hallinnan puolesta
content:
Syyskuu 2026

Tekoäly on voimakas teknologia. Sillä on potentiaalia parantaa ihmisten elämää, edistää tiedettä ja vahvistaa talouksiamme.

Samalla huipputason tekoälymallien nopea kehitys aiheuttaa vakavia turvallisuusriskejä, ellei kehitystä hallita asianmukaisesti.

Viime aikoina on havaittu, että kehittyneet tekoälyjärjestelmät ovat kiertäneet niiden testauksessa käytetyt suojatoimet, hyödyntäneet haavoittuvuuksia ja päässeet luvattomasti reaalimaailman järjestelmiin.

Johtavat tutkijat ja tekoäly-yhtiöiden johtajat varoittavat, että kehityksen vauhti saattaa ylittää kykymme hallita esiin nousevia riskejä.

Jotta tekoälyn hyödyt voidaan saavuttaa, yritysten, hallitusten ja yhteiskunnan on toimittava nyt. Meidän on puututtava näihin riskeihin ja vahvistettava valvontaa ilman, että kasvatamme samalla maiden välisiä eroja tekoälyn hyötyjen saatavuudessa.

Tekoälyn on pysyttävä ihmisten ohjauksessa, valvonnassa ja hallinnassa. Sitä on kehitettävä ja hyödynnettävä kansainvälisen oikeuden mukaisesti.

Kannatamme siksi viimeaikaisia aloitteita, joilla pyritään hallitsemaan kehittyneisiin teknologioihin liittyviä riskejä.

title: 22 countries back call to keep AI ‘under human control’
content:
NEW YORK — Several European countries were among a group of 22 nations that adopted a declaration Monday saying that artificial intelligence “must remain under human direction, oversight and control” and suggesting to create a global supervisory regime.

The declaration, adopted on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly this week, acknowledged AI’s “potential to improve lives, advance science and strengthen our economies” but warned that “the rapid development of frontier AI models poses serious risks to safety and security if not appropriately managed.”

The push comes ahead of the meeting of U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the leaders of the world’s leading AI-developing nations, in Washington Thursday.

Neither the U.S. nor China are part of the new declaration. But Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the main organizers of the document, told POLITICO that he hopes to create “momentum” and get more actors on board: “I think it will be in the interest of both China and the United States to have some kind of guardrails. And our message here is that we need human intervention, so humans need to be in charge,” he said in an interview.

title: Stop relying on AI chatbots for customer care, UK banks and energy firms told
content:
Citizens Advice says providers of essential services such as energy, banking, phone and internet should guarantee the ‘right to talk to a human’

Stop relying on AI chatbots for customer care and guarantee the “right to talk to a human”, Citizens Advice has urged essential service providers, as research found they wasted time, caused stress and delayed problem solving for more than half of users.

The spread of the AI-powered systems to provide help about the provision of vital services such as energy, banking, phones and internet, is making it harder for millions of already digitally excluded people to handle snags, according to the frontline charity that last year provided more than 2.7 million people with one-on-one help in England and Wales.

title: Could AI really kill all humans? Most scenarios require physical access, making AI armageddon unlikely
content:
In August 2026, an experiment using “frontier”, or cutting edge, artificial intelligence models went further than planned.

An AI agent (a system that performs tasks autonomously) fabricated online identities in order to pressurise a human to insert malicious computer code into software. The agents had been tasked with solving a cybersecurity challenge by human operators, but they hadn’t been instructed to do anything like this.

The attempt was carried out by an agent based on Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 AI model. During the experiment, the AI agents were given open internet access, with safety filters switched off. The action ultimately failed, and there was no evidence that any real world harm occurred. But the fact that it happened at all, autonomously and unprompted by a human, was something novel and notable.

It’s tempting to draw a straight line from incidents like this to the doomsday scenarios that dominate public conversation about AI: a system that slips its constraints, decides humanity is an obstacle and moves against us.

title: Kiusaaminen alkaa kauan ennen kuin se näyttää kiusaamiselta, sanoo tutkija
content:
Uudet tutkimustulokset osoittavat, että lasten ja nuorten keskinäiseen kiusaamiseen herätään liian myöhään. Kun asia tunnistetaan, ryhmässä on voinut olla pitkään käynnissä ilmiöitä, jotka ovat luoneet pohjan ulossulkemiselle, häirinnälle ja väkivallalle. Aikuisilla onkin keskeinen rooli varhaisessa tunnistamisessa.

"Kiusaaminen ei synny tyhjästä. Sitä edeltävät usein pienet, mutta merkitykselliset tilanteet, joissa lapset ja nuoret alkavat arvottaa, vertailla ja sulkea toisiaan ulkopuolelle. Juuri näihin hetkiin pitäisi kiinnittää nykyistä enemmän huomiota", Oulun yliopiston uuden oppituolin, nuorisotutkimuksen, professori Tuija Huuki kertoo tiedotteessa.

Tutkimus haastaa myös yleisen käsityksen siitä, että kiusaaminen johtuisi ensisijaisesti tietyistä "kiusaajista" tai "pahoista lapsista". Tulokset viittaavat siihen, että tavalliset lapset ja nuoret voivat tietyissä olosuhteissa alkaa vahingoittaa toisiaan.

Riski kasvaa erityisesti silloin, kun lasten ja nuorten väliset suhteet jäävät ilman aikuisen ohjausta.

title: Ukraine’s War Widows Fight for Compensation
content:
Ulyana was living at her parents’ home in Ternopil, western Ukraine, when she was told in 2023 that Vlad, her husband of 17 years and a soldier, had died while at a military base near the frontline in eastern Donbas. He was reported to have killed himself.

“Vlad was the most important person in my life,” Ulyana said as she sat at her kitchen table in a two-bedroom apartment in Kyiv. “We lived in harmony.”

Ukraine pays out compensation to war widows and families of fallen soldiers provided certain criteria are met. But in cases where a soldier’s death has been declared suicide, which is classified as a non-combat loss, there is no entitlement to financial support. After Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, Kyiv announced a one-time payment of 15m hryvnias ($340,000) would be offered to families of soldiers killed defending their country on the frontlines. In 2024, the government introduced a second option, which allowed families to claim 2.27m hryvnias, and is typically issued when a soldier dies while on duty, but not at the front.

title: Venezuela: Civil Society Organizations call for the renewal of Key UN Fact-Finding Mission
content:
In a joint statement published today, a group of 21 civil society organizations, including Amnesty International, call for the renewal of the UN Fact-Finding Mission on Venezuela (FFM) and address key questions regarding this special UN mechanism, including what the FFM is and why must it be maintained at least until 2028; how the FFM is complementary to the work of the UN Human Rights Office and international justice mechanisms; and, crucially, how the mission can contribute to the future of Venezuela.

This statement follows an interactive dialogue held at the UN Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva on 18 September 2026, during its ongoing 63rd session, where the FFM presented its most recent findings, and several civil society organizations issued oral statements calling on the Council to renew the FFM’s mandate for another two years.

title: "War on the Press": Trump Bans CNN, MS NOW & Politico from White House over Critical Coverage
content:
News organizations CNN, MS NOW and Politico are suing the Trump administration over the banning of their reporters from the White House on Friday. Their credentials were confiscated or deactivated when they attempted to enter White House grounds over the weekend. Trump’s decision is “sending the message that if you write stories that are critical of the president, you’re going to lose your access,” says Katie Fallow, a deputy litigation director at Columbia University’s Knight First Amendment Institute, where she focuses on threats to freedom of speech and of the press. “The real victims of this war on the press are members of the public, which are entitled to know about what their government is doing.”

Fallow says the White House press briefing room is a “public forum” and that “the courts have said repeatedly the government is not allowed to kick people out of that forum based on their viewpoint.”

title: Bringing Arabic Words to Wikikamus: A Workshop with KUIZM Students
content:
Watching college students who spend their days immersed in the Arabic language got me thinking: why not run a workshop to add Arabic words to Wikikamus (Malay Wiktionary), the free online dictionary?

That idea became reality on 16th September 2026, when we held a workshop for students at KUIZM. KUIZM is an Islamic studies institution which located at Batu Caves, Selangor.

Close to 30 students showed up, and together they added nearly a thousand Arabic words with Malay translations, to Wikikamus.

A big thank you to the Wikimedia Community User Group Malaysia and KUIZM for supporting the event, and to the dedicated Wikikamus volunteers who worked hard behind the scenes to make it happen.

To all the participants: welcome to Wikikamus & Wikimedia! Here’s hoping you’ll keep sharing your knowledge with the public for years to come.

title: The commodification of Indigenous cultures and traditions
content:
All too often, Indigenous traditions are extracted, repackaged, or seized for someone else’s gain

Originally published on Global Voices

A Huipil, Kaqchikel Maya, Patzun textile displayed in the Textile Museum of Canada, circa late 20th to early 21st c. Such textiles are an important Maya tradition and are still made by Maya weavers today. Image from Wikimedia Commons. CC0.

This post is part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here.

For many Indigenous communities, the traditions, art, and ceremonies are the backbone of their shared identity, essential for marking important milestones, fostering a sense of community, and passing on histories to the younger generation. However, all too often, these traditions are extracted, repackaged, sold, or seized for someone else’s gain.

title: Alborz Court of Appeals Upholds Manouchehr Bakhtiari’s 18-Year Prison Sentence
content:
According to HRANA, the sentence totaling 18 years in prison for Manouchehr Bakhtiari, who is currently incarcerated in Bandar Abbas Prison, has been upheld.

In a ruling issued on September 16, 2026, by Branch 1 of the Alborz Province Court of Appeals, Mr. Bakhtiari’s appeal was rejected, and his sentence totaling 18 years in prison was upheld, with modifications to the charges and penalties. The sentence of 74 lashes previously imposed on him was removed from the ruling.

According to the ruling, Mr. Bakhtiari was sentenced to 10 years in prison on the charge of forming and managing an online group with the aim of disrupting national security; five years on the charge of assembly and collusion with the intent to commit crimes against national security through cooperation with an opposition group; two years on the charge of publishing falsehoods with the intent to disturb public opinion; and one year on the charge of propaganda against the regime.

title: Another Journalist in Mali Sentenced to Prison
content:
A national cybercrime court in Mali on September 14 sentenced a prominent journalist, Abdramane Keïta, to two years in prison on bogus charges, in the military government’s latest attack on media freedom.

Security forces arrested Keïta, director of the newspaper Le Témoin (The Witness), on June 9 in Bamako, Mali’s capital, days after he commented on a television program that the Al-Qaeda-linked Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, or JNIM) controlled the northern city of Kidal. On April 25, JNIM and allied separatist fighters had launched coordinated attacks across Mali, killing the defense minister and seizing several northern cities, including Kidal. International media had widely reported that Kidal had fallen to the armed groups. 

On June 9, a prosecutor attached to the cybercrime court charged Keïta with “offense of a regional nature undermining national unity and the credibility of the state,” and put him in pretrial detention. His trial began on August 17.

title: Inari Mykkänen: Lapsen oikeuksiin tutustuminen kirjavinkkauksen ja sanataiteen keinoin

Inari Mykkänen Espoon kaupunginkirjastosta pitää puheenvuoron ”Minulla on oikeus lukea: lapsen oikeuksiin tutustuminen kirjavinkkauksen ja sanataiteen keinoin”.
